title: Figma library prune, metadata tagging, and export readiness
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Reduce component noise in the Figma UI Kit by pruning unused variants, apply consistent metadata tags for downstream build/export tooling, and ensure components meet export readiness for the upcoming ui-kit-2025.09 release. This ticket covers audit, pruning plan, metadata taxonomy, autolayout fixes required for export, and publishing checklist.
background: Over the last 18 months the Figma library has accumulated duplicate variants, inconsistent naming, and some components that break our token export scripts. This has led to flaky builds in the component publishing pipeline and unexpected overrides in product apps. Recent infra changes require a smaller, more predictable component surface for downstream codegen and token extraction.
acceptance_criteria: Unused/duplicate variants identified and pruned (list committed to PR)
Metadata tagging taxonomy documented and applied to all top-level components (role, stable/experimental, token-mapping)
All auto-layout issues that prevent frame-based exports fixed (no ambiguous constraints)
Export smoke test passes for token extraction and asset export in staging pipeline
Publish checklist completed and UI Kit published to team library with release notes
tasks: Run component usage audit (Figma plugin + product consumption logs)
Create canonical naming map for primitives and top-level components
Prune flagged variants behind a canary branch in Figma (documented changes)
Apply metadata tags to components: role, stability, token-path
Address autolayout and constraint warnings found by export linter
Coordinate with Engineering to run export smoke test
Draft release notes and update publishing checklist
Ship library publish and verify downstream builds
notes: We will prefer pruning over consolidation where duplicate states are not referenced by product teams
Token-path must match the key names expected by token-extractor v2.1
If a component is used by >=2 product codebases, create a compatibility alias rather than immediate delete
We will keep a rollback snapshot before publish and tag it in Confluence
design_decisions: Adopt explicit 'stability' tag instead of relying on naming conventions to indicate experimental components
Prune variants that are visually identical but differ only by invisible constraints
Standardize on semantic primitive names (e.g., primary-button -> button/primary) to improve token mapping
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental removal of a rarely used but critical variant - mitigation: confirm with product owners and create compatibility aliases
Risk: export tooling mismatch - mitigation: run token-extractor v2.1 locally and coordinate with infra to update if needed
Risk: Figma publish conflicts - mitigation: schedule publish window and inform all design partners via #design-channel
